headline: Gratitude is noticing and appreciating what's good—actively attending to blessings rather than complaints
universal_truth: What you focus on grows; attention to good increases experience of good
fun_facts: Gratitude practice has been shown to improve sleep, health, and relationships
The brain has a negativity bias—we must actively counter with gratitude practice
Writing down three good things daily measurably increases happiness
discussion_questions: What are you grateful for right now?
How does gratitude affect your mood and perspective?
What do you take for granted that deserves appreciation?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Your life contains problems and blessings both. What you notice becomes your experience. Gratitude is the practice of noticing what's good—actively directing attention to what's working rather than only what's broken.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Problems are real and demand attention. Why focus on what's good when things need fixing?

options.text: Gratitude creates accurate perception—problems are real but so are blessings; without gratitude, negativity bias makes life seem worse than it is; gratitude restores balance and generates resilience
options.response: Yes. The brain notices threats more than gifts—survival wiring. But this distorts perception. Gratitude counterbalances, revealing life as it actually is: mixed, not purely negative.
It's related but different—not pretending things are good, but noticing what actually is good alongside problems...

q1.title: Active Practice
q1.script: Gratitude isn't automatic feeling—it's active practice. You choose to notice blessings. You direct attention to what works. This is skill, not sentiment. Practice strengthens it.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Active Practice"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Small Good Things
q2.script: Gratitude doesn't need grand blessings. Coffee, sunshine, a conversation—small goods count. Noticing many small blessings often generates more gratitude than waiting for big ones.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Expression Matters
q3.script: Feeling gratitude is good; expressing it is better. Telling people you appreciate them strengthens relationships and deepens your own gratitude. Express what you feel.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What you focus on grows. Attention to good increases experience of good. Notice and appreciate your blessings.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 345. Tomorrow, we'll explore believing better is possible—hope. Until then, practice noticing what's good.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Gratitude Practice - What's Good Right Now?
growTrack.activity: List three good things from today—large or small. Express gratitude to someone who contributed to your life. Make this a daily practice: notice what's good before reviewing what's wrong.
